chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id, who said:

Abu Abd al-Rahman asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram treating the back of the camel. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He casts off the insects from it and does not bleed it.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دَوَابّ: Insects or small creatures (like flies or ticks)

ai.seo_question: What can a person in Ihram do to treat a camel's back without breaking their ritual state?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility in Ihram disciplines, where the Imam permits treating a camel's back by removing insects as long as the action does not cause bleeding, which would break the state of consecration. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between minor disturbances and those that invalidate the ritual, ensuring that necessary care for animals does not unduly burden the pilgrim.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Abdulla Bin Jabala, from Abdullah Bin Saeed who said,
‘Abu Abdul Rahman asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one in Ihraam treating the back of the camel. So heasws said: ‘He can cast off the insects from it and he should not bleed it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy, from al-‘ Ab has ibn ‘Amir, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sa‘d who has said the following:

“‘Abd al-Rahman once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man’s treating the backside of a camel while in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can throw away bugs but must not make it bleed.’”
